Grayheaded
grā´hĕd´ĕd
adj. (having the hair whitened with age; in Scripture a mark for honour and a call to testify)
English gray + head. The Hebrew is sib or sebah, hoariness — and the law attaches a commandment to it, requiring the young to rise before the hoary head.

Biblical Definition

Samuel steps down grayheaded and appeals to the record: “I am old and grayheaded; and, behold, my sons are with you: and I have walked before you from my childhood unto this day” (1Sa 12:2). Eliphaz claims the advantage of years against Job: “With us are both the grayheaded and very aged men, much elder than thy father” (Job 15:10). And the psalmist prays the one prayer proper to old age: “Now also when I am old and grayheaded, O God, forsake me not; until I have shewed thy strength unto this generation, and thy power to every one that is to come” (Psa 71:18). The law had already commanded the honour: “Thou shalt rise up before the hoary head, and honour the face of the old man, and fear thy God” (Lev 19:32).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines grayheaded as having gray hair, and gray as white with a mixture of black, the color of the hair in old age.

expand to see more

GRAYHEADED, a. Having gray hair; hoary.

GRAY, a. White with a mixture of black; hoary; as gray hairs.

HOARY, a. White or whitish; white or gray with age; as hoary hairs; a hoary head.

Key Scripture

1Sa 12:2 — "And now, behold, the king walketh before you: and I am old and grayheaded; and, behold, my sons are with you: and I have walked before you from my childhood unto this day."

Job 15:10 — "With us are both the grayheaded and very aged men, much elder than thy father."

Psa 71:18 — "Now also when I am old and grayheaded, O God, forsake me not; until I have shewed thy strength unto this generation, and thy power to every one that is to come."

Lev 19:32 — "Thou shalt rise up before the hoary head, and honour the face of the old man, and fear thy God: I am the LORD."

Modern Corruption

Age is commanded honour and is not by itself wisdom, and Job 15 shows the difference by putting the claim in the mouth of a man who was wrong.

expand to see more

Scripture holds two things about the grayhead without embarrassment. The first is that honour is owed: rise up before the hoary head, and fear thy God — the command grounded not in the old man's merit but in the fear of the LORD, which is why it is not negotiable when the old man is difficult. The second is that years do not guarantee understanding. Eliphaz plays the grayheaded card against Job and is rebuked by God in chapter 42; Elihu, the youngest in the room, says plainly that great men are not always wise. Proverbs settles it: the hoary head is a crown of glory if it be found in the way of righteousness. The condition is in the text.

The corruption to name is a culture that has abolished both halves. It does not rise before the hoary head — age is treated as obsolescence, and the old are moved out of sight and out of counsel. And where it does honour age, it often honours it uncritically, as though experience were self-authenticating. Psalm 71 shows the fitting ambition of the aged saint, and it is not comfort but testimony: forsake me not, until I have shewed thy strength unto this generation. The grayhead in Scripture is not retiring. He is still talking about God to the young.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew sib (H7867), to be gray-haired; sebah (H7872), hoary head, old age; zaqen (H2205), old man, elder.

expand to see more

Hebrew sib (H7867) — to be grayheaded; 1 Samuel 12:2, Job 15:10.

Hebrew sebah (H7872) — hoary head, gray hair, old age; Leviticus 19:32, Proverbs 16:31, Isaiah 46:4.

Hebrew zaqen (H2205) — old man, elder; Leviticus 19:32, Deuteronomy 32:7.

Hebrew dor (H1755) — generation; Psalm 71:18, Psalm 145:4.

Hebrew zeroa (H2220) — arm, strength; Psalm 71:18, Isaiah 53:1.

Usage

"“I am old and grayheaded” — Samuel's farewell to Israel."

"“O God, forsake me not; until I have shewed thy strength unto this generation.”"

"“Rise up before the hoary head” — the honour the law commands."
